features.t: Export template (ARM, Bicep, Terraform) on every resource
x: The ARM template is built from the properties Vyomi stores for the resource (system/read-only properties such as provisioningState are dropped by a fixed list, not each resource provider's real schema), so it may omit or include properties real Azure would treat differently.

features.t: Activity log (filters, edit columns, insights, export) on every resource
x: Events are the ARM control-plane mutations Vyomi itself records (write/delete/action on resources); there is no real Azure platform emitting service-health, autoscale, alert or policy events.

Read-only list, exactly like the real Microsoft.Authorization/classicAdministrators API (the legacy co-administrator model is retired): a modern subscription shows only its Account Administrator / Service Administrator, which in Vyomi is the single simulated signed-in user. Adding or removing classic administrators is not possible and is not modelled.

Health is derived from the resource's own stored state (failed provisioning, a stopped/deallocated VM or stopped AKS cluster); Vyomi runs no Azure platform, so there are never platform outages, planned maintenance or a health-history feed — the history section is always empty.

Recommendations come from a small fixed rule set over each resource's stored configuration (Key Vault soft delete / purge protection, storage secure transfer / public blob access / TLS, SQL TLS, NSG open SSH/RDP, App Service HTTPS only, ACR admin user) — all in the Security category. Cost, Reliability and Performance recommendations need real utilisation telemetry, which Vyomi does not have, so none are produced.

Settings are stored and validated exactly as the real Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings resource requires (at least one destination; a storage destination must be a real resource), but logs and metrics are never delivered to the workspace, storage account or event hub — there is no telemetry pipeline.

The graph is drawn from the real ARM resource list of the resource group; an edge exists only where a stored property of one resource holds another resource's id. Layout is a fixed circle (no drag, zoom, or expand-by-type), and cross-resource-group relationships are not shown.

features.t: Browse-grid Open query (Resource Graph) and Assign tags
x: Open query runs a minimal Kusto subset (tables Resources and ResourceContainers; where with =~ / == / contains, project, limit, count) evaluated over Vyomi's ARM resource store — no joins, summarize, extend or order by. The console posts to the subscription-prefixed path; real Azure Resource Graph is tenant-level (Nano also answers that form).

features.t: Support requests (Microsoft.Support) on every blade, filed with Vyomi
x: Requests are real Microsoft.Support/supportTickets (services, problem classifications, severity, contact details, communications, close) with validation and a Vyomi Support acknowledgement, and are stored in the simulator. Delivery to the Vyomi portal support queue is not wired yet: each ticket reports properties.vyomiDelivery = recorded-locally, and no human replies arrive here. Support plans, phone callbacks and Microsoft's own engineers do not exist.

features.t: Alerts, Metrics, Logs, Insights and Workbooks on every resource
x: REAL: Microsoft.Insights/metricAlerts scoped to the resource (stored and validated like Azure's; Evaluate now computes a rule against the real metric on demand), metric definitions + values, Log Analytics queries over the resource's own Activity log (AzureActivity), and Microsoft.Insights/workbooks linked to the resource.

features.t: Diagnose and solve problems (AKS, API Management, App Configuration, Cognitive Services, App Service)
x: Detectors (core/azure_diagnose_core.py) are computed from the resource's live record, its child resources and its own Activity log: provisioning/power state, capacity, version support, network exposure, authentication and recent failed operations. There is no platform telemetry behind a simulator (no real node health, gateway traffic or model latency), so no detector reads invented metrics, and there are no auto-run remediation actions or AI troubleshooter.
